A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic calibration experiments, Type-I error and power analyses, and image–text and video–language representation analyses in Section 6 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds real-network width analysis, shared-input synthetic experiments and quantitative scaling analyses in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The proposed scalar and aggregation-aware permutation calibration procedures remain unchanged, including Equations (8)–(17). The revised pseudocode explicitly specifies the ceiling order statistic already required by v1's equations; it does not introduce a new calibration algorithm.

E1.justification: WIT image–text and PVD video–language coverage remains. v2 adds within-vision comparisons using the same WIT images and a synthetic scenario where independent random linear networks or MLPs process shared inputs (Appendices E.5 and E.7). These are limited extensions of the evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: The image–text raw-versus-calibrated comparison now includes RV, SVCCA and Procrustes on DINOv2 (v2 Figure 20); v1 evaluated these metrics in synthetic experiments but did not report this real-data comparison. The alternative calibration approaches and the debiased-CKA and dep-cols CKA comparators remain.

E3.justification: Appendix B substantively revises reported evaluation definitions, including PWCCA weighting, cycle-kNN, CKNNA, unbiased HSIC and Procrustes normalization. v2 also expands VideoMAE checkpoint settings, adds Pearson trend summaries and continuous language-performance fits, and specifies a reduced DINOv2 comparison subset. The formula revisions establish changes in the documented protocol, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds fixed-sample real-network width analysis, robustness to shared-input representation generators, rank-versus-continuous-capability analysis, and fine-tuned versus non-fine-tuned video comparisons. These substantially extend tests of the calibration argument. The video mKNN k=50 analysis in v1 Figure 19 is absent from v2 Figure 25; the image–text neighborhood-size analysis remains.

E5.justification: The image–text significance analysis reports K=200 permutations in v1 Appendix F.7 and K=500 in v2 Appendix E.8, changing the stated minimum attainable p-value from approximately 0.005 to 0.002. The existing permutation-budget analysis across 50 random seeds is retained.

E6.justification: v2 adds the real-network width correlation r=0.88 and Table 2's raw-versus-calibrated capability correlations, including linear CKA 0.86 versus 0.45 and mKNN k=10 0.85 versus 0.84. Figure 12's calibrated-minus-dep-cols differences under signal change from positive in v1 to negative in v2. Additional video checkpoint results and revised synthetic plots further change the reported evidence; these are not same-setting performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: v2 adds Proposition C.5 and its proof: with genuine shared signal and fixed sample size, sample linear CKA approaches one as width grows although population CKA remains rho squared. It also substantively revises several formal metric definitions in Appendix B. The existing permutation-validity, depth-confounding and neighborhood-null proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contribution claims remain: width and depth confound similarity measurements, permutation calibration addresses these effects, and local neighborhood convergence survives more strongly than global spectral convergence. v2 supplies additional support and qualifications without redefining the principal method or Aristotelian hypothesis.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes CCA-family rank-deficiency effects from covariance-energy inflation and identifies RSA as an exception to width-driven null drift. It reverses the dep-cols interpretation from signal attenuation to excessive scores under signal and adds the limitation that similarity lacks a ground-truth scale. The exchangeability limitation is retained and relocated, rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: v2 discloses class-token extraction for vision and mean-token pooling for language, clarifies non-interpolated quantiles in both algorithms, and expands implementation-cost information. Appendix D describes cached structures, GPU-batched decompositions and GTX 1080 Ti timings of 20 ms for linear CKA and 52 ms for mKNN per layer pair at K=200. Code and project access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds literature on multimodal alignment, layer-search practice, similarity benchmarking, random matrices and brain alignment, including Gröger, Kapoor, ReSi, Livan, Schaeffer and Soni. It more explicitly relates aggregation calibration to maxT and explains compatibility with prior convergence research. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 adds explanatory 'What it measures' paragraphs throughout the metric appendix, expands the conclusion, relocates the exchangeability discussion and makes localized wording and bibliographic edits. Most of the main narrative and section sequence remain intact; the added scientific material does not constitute a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds a quantitative trend table, real-network and shared-input plots, additional metric comparisons, and continuous-performance plots with fitted lines. It redraws or rescales several synthetic figures and restructures the video figure to distinguish checkpoint variants while removing its k=50 row. These display changes extend substantially beyond relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The new shared-signal width proof, quantitative scaling summaries and clearer implementation disclosures strengthen justification and reproducibility. v1 already contained substantial signal, noise, locality and significance-level analyses, so the gains mainly refine an established argument. The expanded video checkpoint comparison adds useful evidence, although removing its k=50 slice slightly narrows robustness coverage.
